admission.justification: Losing uncommitted parked or owner-written bytes, or retiring their sole restoration authority after a misleading proof, is a plausible costly error; the named transaction witnesses check the obligation before such loss can be accepted.

applicability: Pre-destructive cancellation assessment and save-first preservation of unattributable code/memory worktree and index state.
conditions: Worktree bytes alone do not authorize discarding differing index stages.
A crash-window tree earns fingerprints only from exact scratch replay, including converted structural merge, paired code and owner.
Unproved attribution is named truthfully and saved before cancellation proceeds; neither saved bytes nor a failed proof establish transaction ownership.

Fresh saves use durable atomic writes and record SHA-256 of the written payload; recovery of prior completed manifests reopens and verifies their named bytes. Fresh-save durability is not an independent reread of every artifact.
A failed save or discard retains safe recovery state; public cancel retry does not retire the original stash prematurely.
exclusions: Only the memory-side derived cache is outside substantive work.
A manually resolved retained tree is owner state unless exact ownership is proved.

evidence: Synced freeze 231622b2c7e272e7ca182ec28d3da61ca1749e0f + tracked diff d4c93e6a94ef056ca4d5eb77d4c05d73eac6062654729e2cb979d0cfd870141f (S2 documentary correction of the S list: stale symbol spellings and the rule-1 inventory rationale corrected, all other producer fields identical); ResumedConvertedMemoryMergeTests (2 tests) in test_sync_parked_candidate.py.

statement: Cancellation durably saves later or unproved owner state in product-owned files before discard and rollback; it never blesses that state as transaction output and a save or discard stop retains journal and restoration authority for retry.
